record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Let HS = sum_{k>=0} H(k)t^k be the Hilbert series of a ring or variety, and let its unrefined Laurent expansion be HS = sum_{i>=0} gamma_i/(1-t)^(d-i), where d is the Krull dimension. What are the mathematical and physical interpretations of all Laurent coefficients gamma_i of an arbitrary Hilbert series?

evidence.quote: Question 1. What are the mathematical and physical interpretations of all the Laurent coefficients of any HS?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be a finitely generated graded commutative algebra over a field (or, more generally, the coordinate ring of an affine variety) of Krull dimension d, and let
   HS(t) = sum_{k>=0} H(k) t^k
be its Hilbert series, where H(k) is the dimension of the k-th graded piece. Expand HS(t) as a Laurent series about t = 1 in the form
   HS(t) = sum_{i>=0} gamma_i / (1 - t)^{d-i},
defining a sequence of rational coefficients gamma_0, gamma_1, gamma_2, ... .

It is known that, in favorable cases, gamma_0 equals the degree of the underlying variety (and, when the variety is the affine cone over a Sasaki-Einstein manifold, equals a normalized volume of the base, related to central charges of an associated supersymmetric gauge theory), and that low-order coefficients gamma_0, gamma_1 can sometimes be expressed in terms of the a-invariant of R or, in the case of an invariant ring under a finite group, in terms of the group order and the number of pseudoreflections.

Problem. Provide a general mathematical interpretation, and (when the algebra arises as a Coulomb-branch / Higgs-branch / moduli-space chiral ring of a supersymmetric quiver gauge theory) a corresponding physical interpretation, of every Laurent coefficient gamma_i, i >= 0, of an arbitrary Hilbert series HS(t).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on quiver gauge theory. While interpretations are known for the leading coefficient gamma_0 (degree of the variety; volume of the Sasaki-Einstein base in the Gorenstein case) and partial results exist for gamma_1 (related to the a-invariant or, for invariant rings, to group order and pseudoreflections), no general interpretation of all gamma_i appears in the literature, and the problem is still listed as open in subsequent work.

status_evidence.snippet: Question 1. What are the mathematical and physical interpretations of all the Laurent coefficients of any HS?
status_evidence.claim: The question of interpreting all Laurent coefficients of a Hilbert series is explicitly raised as an open question.

status_evidence.title: The Laurent Coefficients of the Hilbert Series of a Gorenstein Algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the Laurent coefficients of the Hilbert series of a Gorenstein algebra, giving partial interpretations.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for the Gorenstein case, but a complete interpretation of all coefficients is not given.
